criteria.name: Introduction: mission concept and rationale. Include the following required information: What is the spacecraft's primary mission? Why is the mission needed? How many spacecraft are used and why? Who are the users (operator and customers)?
criteria.reasoning: All required information addressed in detail: primary mission, rationale with cited literature, single-spacecraft justification, operator and customers. Well referenced; only minor depth lacking on user needs analysis.

evidence.quote: The primary mission of ZYZZsat is to image the whole Great Barrier Reef in visible bands at 5 m resolution
The operator is the Australian Institute of Marine Science (AIMS)... The customers are the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Authority
One satellite is therefore used. This also simplifies communications, reduces cost

criteria.name: Main body: mission design. Present a summary of the mission design using software and/or hand calculations as appropriate. Include relevant screenshots and software files in the main body of the report and/or appendix. Include the following information: Where will it launch from, and using which launch vehicle? Why did you choose this option? What type of orbit will you use? What are its characteristics and orbital elements? Will you need to perform any orbital maneuvers? Which ground control facilities will you use? How often will your spacecraft be able to communicate with ground control? How long will the mission last, and what are your plans for EOL?
criteria.reasoning: Comprehensive, accurate design: launch site/vehicle with justified trade, hand calculations (azimuth, J2 sun-sync inclination, decay) verified correct, STK screenshots, access tables, data budget, EOL plan. Link budget admittedly missing, a minor gap.

evidence.quote: The baseline is an SSMS rideshare flight on Vega C from Kourou in early 2025
cos i = −0.1355, so i = 97.79°. This agrees with the STK value of 97.7924°
There are six passes each day... the mean pass lasts 580.8 s, or 9.7 minutes
With a 4 m² sail the satellite re-enters about two years after the end of the mission

criteria.name: Conclusion
criteria.reasoning: Conclusions follow directly from the evidence and include honest limitations and next-phase actions; slightly more quantitative summary would make it fully accomplished.

evidence.quote: A 600 km sun-synchronous orbit at 97.79° inclination gives the same morning lighting on every pass

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Clear structure, concise executive summary, numbered/labelled figures and tables, consistent formatting, in-text citations [1]–[15] matching bibliography. Minor: some references (e.g. [4], [15]) are loosely specified.

evidence.quote: This report presents the design of ZYZZsat... a single Earth observation microsatellite for monitoring coral bleaching
Figure 2: Inclination required for a sun-synchronous orbit as a function of altitude.

technical_issues.issue: X-band link budget not performed (acknowledged by student); 50 Mbit/s assumed feasible.
Vega C unflown at time of writing; fallback acknowledged but adds risk.
Decay estimate uses single mean density; student correctly notes solar-cycle factor-of-ten uncertainty.

overall: Excellent, technically sound mission design report. All task requirements addressed with verified hand calculations, STK evidence and files, clear structure and referencing. Minor gaps: link budget and some loosely specified references.

feedback.summary: Excellent work on the ZYZZsat mission design report. All required elements are addressed with verified hand calculations, STK evidence and clear referencing. To reach the very top of the rubric, add the X-band link budget, tighten loosely specified references, and make the conclusion more quantitative.
next_steps: Complete the X-band link budget for Section 2.4 to substantiate the assumed 50 Mbit/s downlink, showing margin for the six daily passes.
Quantify the four limitations listed in your conclusion (e.g. decay uncertainty range, link margin) so conclusions are directly traceable to evidence.
Replace loosely specified references such as [4] and [15] with fully cited sources, and consider a brief user-needs analysis for AIMS/GBRMPA in Section 1.

criteria.C1: Accomplished (9/10). Your introduction thoroughly covers the primary mission (5 m GBR imaging), rationale with literature, single-spacecraft justification, and operator/customers. Next level: add a short user-needs analysis showing how AIMS and GBRMPA requirements drive the 5 m resolution and revisit choices.
criteria.C2: Accomplished (9/10). Comprehensive design: justified Vega C/Kourou trade, verified J2 sun-sync inclination (97.79°), STK access tables, data budget and EOL plan. Next level: perform the X-band link budget you flagged as missing, and discuss quantitatively how the Vega C unflown-status risk affects your fallback choice.
criteria.C3: Accomplished (8/10). Conclusions follow from your evidence and honestly state limitations and next-phase actions. Next level: summarise key quantitative results (orbit elements, pass statistics, decay time, data volumes) in the conclusion so it stands alone as a design summary.
criteria.C4: Accomplished (9/10). Clear structure, concise executive summary, well-labelled figures/tables, and in-text citations [1]–[15] matching the bibliography. Next level: ensure every reference is fully specified (e.g. [4], [15]) so all sources are independently traceable.
